parsed.summary: This paper presents MaxKernel, a multi-agent framework designed to automate and optimize TPU kernel engineering. It supports three orchestration paradigms: Human-in-the-Loop, Autonomous Loop, and Graph-Based Autonomous Search. Evaluating on JaxBench and real-world workloads, MaxKernel achieves a 1.58× geometric mean speedup over XLA baselines and outperforms human-written kernels on production workloads.

chk_problem.value: Designing and authoring high-performance custom kernels for accelerators is a complex task requiring deep hardware-level expertise.
chk_problem.paper_quote: Designing and authoring high-performance custom kernels for accelerators is a complex task that requires deep hardware-level expertise.

chk_method.value: MaxKernel, a multi-agent system implementing three paradigms: Human-in-the-Loop, Autonomous Loop, and Graph-Based Autonomous Search.
chk_method.paper_quote: In this work, we present MaxKernel, a multi-agent system that implements three distinct paradigms for TPU kernel development: (1) a Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) agent for collaborative, step-by-step design; (2) an Autonomous (Auto) agent that executes a fully automated, metric/trace-driven optimization loop; and (3) a Graph-Based Autonomous Search that scales the Auto agent for global exploration of the design space.

chk_data.value: JaxBench, a suite of 50 diverse TPU kernel tasks, and real-world workloads from state-of-the-art open-source models.
chk_data.paper_quote: We evaluate MaxKernel on JaxBench, a comprehensive suite of 50 diverse kernel tasks for TPUs, alongside complex, real-world workloads from state-of-the-art open-source models.

chk_setup.value: Empirical evaluations conducted on TPU v6e hardware using MaxKernel's dedicated evaluation harness.
chk_setup.paper_quote: All empirical evaluations are conducted on TPU v6e hardware using MaxKernel’s dedicated evaluation harness.

chk_primary_result.value: MaxKernel achieves a 1.58× geometric mean speedup across the JAXBench workloads.
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: MaxKernel successfully bridges the gap between static LLM code generation and high-performance kernel engineering, achieving a 1.58× geometric mean speedup across the JAXBench workloads.

chk_secondary_result.value: On eight production workloads, MaxKernel achieves a 2.32× geometric mean speedup over reference code, outperforming human-written ones (2.02×).
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Furthermore, on the eight production kernels where human-written kernels exist, MaxKernel achieves a 2.32× geometric mean speedup over the reference code, outperforming human-written ones (2.02×).

chk_baseline.value: The standard XLA compiler baseline, as well as expert-written, hand-tuned Pallas references and zero-shot Best-of-N.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: To measure aggregate performance, we report the (3) geometric mean speedup across all tasks relative to the standard XLA compiler baseline (with performance regressions floored at 1.0x).

chk_conclusion.value: Agentic systems can successfully handle the complexities of low-level accelerator programming.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: MaxKernel demonstrates that agentic systems can successfully handle the complexities of low-level accelerator programming.

chk_limitation.value: The Auto Agent performs linear, iterative improvements but remains susceptible to local optima.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: While the Auto Agent performs linear, iterative improvements, it remains susceptible to local optima.
